properties.text: encode_internal_node must only accept nodes of type None, LeafNode, ExtensionNode, or BranchNode. For any other type, the function must raise an AssertionError and never return a value.

For any node passed to encode_internal_node, if rlp.encode(unencoded_form) produces output strictly less than 32 bytes, the function must return the unencoded form (the raw tuple/list/bytes). If the encoded output is 32 bytes or more, the function must return keccak256(encoded).

encode_node must require a non-None storage_root when the node is an Account instance. Specifically, the assertion (storage_root is not None) must hold before encode_account is called. Violation must raise AssertionError.

For any node type not explicitly handled by encode_node (i.e., not Account, LegacyTransaction, Receipt, Withdrawal, U256, or Bytes), the function must delegate to previous_trie.encode_node(node, storage_root) and return its result without modification.

copy_trie must produce a new Trie object such that modifications to the copy's _data dictionary do not affect the original's _data dictionary, and vice versa. Specifically, adding or removing keys in the copy must not change the set of keys in the original.
After trie_set(trie, key, value) where value equals trie.default, the key must not exist in trie._data. Formally: forall trie, key: trie_set(trie, key, trie.default) implies (key not in trie._data).

Setting a key to the default value via trie_set must be equivalent to deletion. Formally: for all keys k, trie_set(trie, k, trie.default) followed by trie_get(trie, k) must return trie.default, and k must be absent from trie._data.
trie_get must return trie.default for any key not present in trie._data. Formally: forall trie, key: (key not in trie._data) implies trie_get(trie, key) == trie.default.
common_prefix_length(a, b) must return a value in the range [0, min(len(a), len(b))]. It must never return a negative value or a value exceeding the length of either input.
For the return value r of common_prefix_length(a, b), for all indices j where 0 <= j < r, it must hold that a[j] == b[j]. That is, all elements before position r are pairwise equal.

All nibble values in the input to nibble_list_to_compact must be in the range [0, 15]. If any nibble value is outside this range, the compact encoding is undefined and the output is potentially corrupted.

The high nibble of the first byte of nibble_list_to_compact output must correctly encode both the is_leaf flag and the parity of the input length. Specifically: if even length, first byte high nibble = 2*is_leaf; if odd length, first byte high nibble = 2*is_leaf + 1.
The output length of nibble_list_to_compact must equal ceil((len(x) + 1) / 2), where x is the input nibble list. This ensures the compact encoding has the precise expected size.
bytes_to_nibble_list must produce output of length exactly 2 * len(input). For any input of n bytes, the output must contain exactly 2n nibbles.
Every nibble in the output of bytes_to_nibble_list must be in the range [0, 15]. Formally: forall i in [0, 2*len(input)): output[i] >= 0 and output[i] <= 15.

bytes_to_nibble_list and nibble_list_to_compact must form an invertible pair (modulo compact header). For any byte sequence b, nibble_list_to_compact(bytes_to_nibble_list(b), is_leaf=False) must produce a compact encoding from which b can be recovered by stripping the header.

All encoded values in the output of _prepare_trie must be non-empty (not equal to b''). If any encoded value is empty, _prepare_trie must raise an AssertionError before including it in the output mapping.
When trie.secured is True, _prepare_trie must hash all keys with keccak256 before converting them to nibble lists. When trie.secured is False, keys must be used as-is without hashing.

When _prepare_trie encounters an Account value, the get_storage_root callback must be provided (not None). The function must call get_storage_root(Address(preimage)) and pass the result to encode_node. Omission of get_storage_root for Account values must cause a failure.
When trie._data is empty, root(trie) must return EMPTY_TRIE_ROOT, which equals keccak256(rlp.encode(b'')). This must hold regardless of trie.secured or trie.default values.

The return value of root() must always be exactly 32 bytes. Whether the root node's RLP encoding is less than 32 bytes (triggering keccak256 hashing) or 32 bytes or more (returning Root(root_node)), the final result must be a 32-byte value.

When the RLP encoding of root_node is 32 bytes or more, root_node must already be a Bytes (hash) value returned from encode_internal_node. The root() function must return it directly as Root(root_node) without additional hashing.
patricialize({}, level) must return None for any value of level. An empty input mapping must never produce a LeafNode, ExtensionNode, or BranchNode.

When patricialize receives a single-element mapping {key: value}, it must return a LeafNode with rest_of_key = key[level:] and the value from the mapping. It must never produce an ExtensionNode or BranchNode for a single entry.

When all keys in the input to patricialize share a common prefix of length > 0 at the given level, the function must return an ExtensionNode containing that shared prefix and a recursively constructed subnode.

When the keys in the input to patricialize have no shared prefix (common prefix length == 0), the function must return a BranchNode with exactly 16 subnodes (one per nibble value 0-15), each constructed by recursively patricializing the subset of keys with that nibble at position level.

In patricialize, when a key's length equals the current level (indicating a branch value position), the value must not be an instance of Account, Receipt, or Uint. If such a type is found at a branch value position, the function must raise an AssertionError.

Every recursive call in patricialize must strictly increase the level parameter. Formally: if patricialize(obj, level) calls patricialize(sub_obj, level'), then level' > level. This guarantees termination since level is bounded by the maximum key length.

The RLP encoder must produce canonical, deterministic output. For any two invocations rlp.encode(x) and rlp.encode(y), if x == y then rlp.encode(x) == rlp.encode(y) (byte-for-byte). Furthermore, the encoding must match the Ethereum RLP specification exactly.

keccak256 must be collision-resistant: for any two distinct inputs x != y, keccak256(x) != keccak256(y) with overwhelming probability (2^{-128} collision probability). Additionally, keccak256 must produce consistent output: keccak256(x) must return the same 32-byte value for the same input x across all invocations.

The get_storage_root callback, when invoked with an address, must return a 32-byte Root value. The trie implementation asserts (storage_root is not None) but does not validate the root's semantic correctness. A corrupted storage root must be detectable only by higher-level verification.

The previous fork's encode_node implementation must produce output that is semantically compatible with the current fork. Specifically, for any node type delegated to previous_trie.encode_node, the returned encoding must be a valid RLP-encoded representation that, when used in the trie, produces consensus-compatible roots.

trie._data must only be modified through trie_set. No external code path may directly insert, delete, or modify entries in trie._data. Direct manipulation would violate the default-value deletion invariant (INV-006/INV-007) and could leave entries with value == trie.default (ghost entries).

copy_trie's shallow copy is safe only because trie values are immutable (frozen) objects. Formally: for all values v in trie._data.values(), v must be an immutable type. If mutable objects are stored, modifications after copy would affect both the original and the copy.

The iteration order of trie._data.items() in _prepare_trie must not affect the final computed root. For any permutation of the same set of (key, value) pairs, patricialize must produce an identical Merkle tree structure yielding the same root hash.

In secured tries (trie.secured == True), user-supplied keys must be hashed with keccak256 before insertion into the trie's nibble-key mapping. This must prevent adversarial key ordering attacks where an attacker crafts keys with long common prefixes to create deeply unbalanced trie structures.

The type dispatch in encode_node must handle all expected node types explicitly via isinstance checks. For any input node, exactly one code path must be taken: Account, (LegacyTransaction, Receipt, Withdrawal, U256), Bytes, or the fallback to previous_trie.encode_node. No input may cause encode_node to silently produce incorrect output.

If the get_storage_root callback returns an incorrect storage root for a given address, the encoded account will embed a wrong storage root hash, which will propagate into the state root. The only mitigation is that get_storage_root is provided by the trusted state module.

The get_storage_root callback must not be substitutable by an untrusted party. The callback must be constructed within the trusted state module and passed directly to _prepare_trie/root(). No external actor may inject a custom callback.

The previous fork's encode_node must produce deterministic, canonical encodings identical to what the current fork would produce for the same node type. Any inconsistency between the previous fork's and current fork's encoding of the same logical node would cause a consensus split.

Every node type introduced in a fork must be explicitly handled by either the current fork's encode_node or a previous fork's encode_node in the fallback chain. A type that falls through all dispatch chains without being handled must result in an error, not silent misencoding.

The 32-byte threshold check in encode_internal_node must produce identical results across all Ethereum implementations. Since this check depends on the exact byte length of RLP output, the RLP encoding must be canonical (no alternative valid encodings for the same data).

The information boundary at the 32-byte threshold is by design: nodes with encoded size < 32 bytes are embedded inline (revealing their structure), while nodes >= 32 bytes are replaced by their keccak256 hash (hiding their structure). This behavior must be consistent and deterministic.

keccak256 must produce identical output for identical input across all three critical usage paths: (1) key hashing in secured tries, (2) node hashing when encoded size >= 32 bytes, (3) root node hashing when encoded size < 32 bytes. Any inconsistency breaks consensus.

keccak256 must provide at least 128-bit collision resistance. Two different addresses must not hash to the same trie key in a secured trie. If keccak256 collision resistance were broken, an attacker could craft two addresses that map to the same trie key, overwriting one account's state with another's.

The trie root computation must be fully deterministic. For any two tries T1 and T2 with identical sets of (key, value) pairs, root(T1) must equal root(T2) bit-for-bit, regardless of insertion order, internal state, or execution environment. Non-determinism would allow block producers to claim different valid roots.

The computational cost of root() must be bounded. For n entries in the trie, the root computation must complete in O(n * log(n)) time and O(n) space. Gas costs for state-modifying operations must limit n to a manageable size per block.

Without key hashing (secured == False), an attacker could choose keys with long common prefixes that force the creation of deeply nested extension nodes, degrading trie operations to O(n) per lookup. All state and storage tries must use secured=True to mitigate this.

No entry in trie._data may have a value equal to trie.default. The presence of such a 'ghost entry' would cause it to be encoded and included in the Merkle tree, producing an incorrect root that includes a logically-deleted key.

Direct manipulation of trie._data (bypassing trie_set) must not occur in any code path. The underscore prefix convention on _data is the only enforcement mechanism. Any direct write to _data could insert values that violate the default-value deletion invariant, leading to state corruption.

For any trie T and any sequence of trie_set operations S1, S2, ..., Sn, the resulting trie state must depend only on the final value assigned to each key, not on the order or intermediate values. Formally: if two sequences of operations produce the same final (key -> value) mapping, root() must return the same hash.

trie_get(trie, key) must return the value most recently set by trie_set(trie, key, value) for any key where value != trie.default. If trie_set was never called for a key, or the most recent call set it to trie.default, trie_get must return trie.default.
encode_internal_node(None) must return b'' (empty bytes). This is the canonical encoding for an absent node in the trie and is critical for branch nodes that have empty slots.
For encode_node, when the input is of type Bytes, the function must return the node unchanged (identity function). No encoding, hashing, or transformation may be applied to Bytes-typed nodes.

The encode_account function, when called from encode_node with a valid Account and a non-None storage_root, must produce a deterministic encoding that includes the account's nonce, balance, storage_root, and code_hash in the canonical order specified by the Ethereum account RLP structure.

For a LeafNode passed to encode_internal_node, the unencoded form must be a tuple (compact_key, value) where compact_key is nibble_list_to_compact(rest_of_key, True). The is_leaf flag in the compact encoding must be True.

For an ExtensionNode passed to encode_internal_node, the unencoded form must be a tuple (compact_key, subnode) where compact_key is nibble_list_to_compact(key_segment, False). The is_leaf flag in the compact encoding must be False.

For a BranchNode passed to encode_internal_node, the unencoded form must be a list of exactly 17 elements: 16 subnodes (one per nibble 0-15) followed by the branch value. The list must always have this exact structure.

The empty trie root constant EMPTY_TRIE_ROOT must equal keccak256(rlp.encode(b'')). This value must be identical across all Ethereum implementations and forks. Any discrepancy in this constant would cause consensus failures on empty storage tries.

common_prefix_length must be symmetric-adjacent: if common_prefix_length(a, b) returns r, and r < min(len(a), len(b)), then a[r] != b[r]. That is, the first position after the common prefix must be a point of divergence (when both sequences have elements at that position).

The _prepare_trie function must produce a bijective mapping from nibble-encoded keys to encoded values. No two distinct original keys may map to the same nibble key. In secured mode, this is guaranteed by keccak256 collision resistance. In unsecured mode, the input keys must be distinct.

For any two logically distinct states S1 and S2 (where at least one key maps to a different value), root(trie(S1)) must not equal root(trie(S2)). The Merkle Patricia Trie must be collision-free: distinct states must produce distinct roots (with overwhelming cryptographic probability).

copy_trie must preserve the secured flag, the default value, and all (key, value) pairs exactly. Formally: for all keys k, trie_get(copy_trie(trie), k) == trie_get(trie, k), and copy.secured == trie.secured, and copy.default == trie.default.

After copy_trie, the root of the copy must equal the root of the original. Formally: root(copy_trie(trie)) == root(trie). This ensures that trie snapshots used for rollback produce consistent state roots.
